### The Memory of Metal

Metal is not a passive canvas. Silver is an active collaborator, possessing memory, mood, and boundaries. When subjected to intense heat and the rhythmic pressure of the hammer, it reacts, remembers, and holds its form. It records every choice made in the quiet studio. In our London home workshop, we embrace this dialogue daily.

### The Lost-Wax Casting Discipline

Every ring, earring, and cuff we craft relies on the ancient discipline of lost-wax casting. This technique, preserved across millennia, begins by hand-carving a scale model of the structural concept in jewellers' wax. The tactile nature of wax carving allows us to refine the edges, softening computational severity with natural warmth. Once cast, the piece faces the crucible of finishing. We choose not to erase the toolmarks entirely. They tell the story of creation, serving as physical proof of a dedicated human touch.
